title: Fleet Synthetic Conformance Lab and Customer Acceptance Script
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a reproducible lab and scripted acceptance flow that verifies Dedicated fleets meet negotiated throughput guarantees and autoscaling behavior before customer signoff.
objective: Provide a deterministic, tenant-aware synthetic load harness and measurement methodology that engineering, solutions, and customers can run to validate throughput SLAs and autoscaler safety policies.
scope: Design and implement: a synthetic workload generator that simulates mixed request types and KV cache states; a deterministic replay mode for customer traces; a conformance runner that asserts throughput, p99/p95 latency windows, and autoscaler scaling actions; and a customer-facing acceptance script with clear pass/fail criteria and artifacts (plots, trace IDs, replay logs).
methodology: 1) Define canonical workload profiles (burst-heavy, steady-sustain, mixed-latency) from production telemetry. 2) Implement tenant-aware injectors that parameterize token distribution, prompt lengths, and cache hit ratios. 3) Run golden-run deterministic replays and stochastic sweeps across seed sets. 4) Collect metrics from serving runtime, autoscaler controller, and host telemetry. 5) Normalize and compute SLA conformance metrics and generate a signed acceptance bundle for customers.
test_suite_components: tenant-aware synthetic injector with header-tenant and api-key mapping
deterministic-replay engine that replays recorded traces with time-warp control
autoscaler-simulator to predict and then verify scaling decisions
continuous-benchmark-runner with warmup, ramp, sustain, and cool-down phases
artifact-packager that bundles metrics, traces, and failure repro steps
metrics: throughput_rps (requests per second) by model and route
autoscaler_reaction_time (seconds from threshold to scale action)
scale_step_effectiveness (throughput delta per added GPU node)
acceptance_criteria: Sustained throughput meets or exceeds committed RPS for 30 minutes during sustain window
p95 latency remains below the SLA threshold for the sustain window
Tail latency degradation under burst does not exceed 2x baseline within 99th percentile
Autoscaler performs at most two corrective scale steps within a 5 minute burst recovery window and stabilizes without oscillation
No unhandled 5xx class errors introduced by the test (error rate < 0.1%)
Deterministic replay reproduces customer 95th percentile within 10% of original trace metrics
Artifacts (plots, traces, config used) are generated and uploaded to the acceptance bundle link
test_plan: Phase A: Local lab validation with small fleet replica and synthetic workloads. Phase B: Staging fleet run using production-like instance types and mixed tenants. Phase C: Customer-facing acceptance session where customer provides a representative trace or accepts canonical workload. Each phase has pre-checks, warmup, ramp, sustain (30min), and cool-down. Run logging includes deterministic seed values and telemetry snapshots.
test_schedule: Week 1: Implement workload profiles and injector, unit tests
Week 2: Build deterministic replay engine and autoscaler simulator
Week 3: End-to-end lab runs and metric dashboarding
Week 4: Staging runs and runbook finalization
Week 5: Pilot customer acceptance with two beta customers
rollout_plan: Merge feature branch behind a feature flag. Enable in canary staging for a single fleet. Validate metrics and iterate. Open access to Solutions Engineering for pilot customers. Publish acceptance script and playbook in Console onboarding area and link to customer-facing runbook. After two successful pilots, remove flag and make available as standard verification suite for Dedicated onboarding.
dependencies: infra-k8s-autoscaler-v2 rollout for making test autoscaler policies available
risks: Synthetic workload may not faithfully reproduce edge caches (leading to false positives)
Autoscaler simulator divergence from production controller behavior if controller tuning changes
Running large sustained loads in staging may impact other teams if isolation not enforced
Customer traces may contain PII and require redaction before replay
notes: Prefer using pre-provisioned dedicated fleets with isolated tenant namespaces for staging runs to avoid noisy neighbors.
We will instrument a lightweight tracer that tags requests with synthetic-run-id to make artifact correlation deterministic.
Coordinate with Solutions Engineering to collect representative customer traces and obtain consent for replay tests. Use redaction tool if necessary.
